text.p: Turkish market opened 27.3 trillion lira long on Friday and the central bank withdrew idle cash at close after demand caused by liquidity requirements ahead of the weekend was met, bankers said.

The central bank drained 11.9 trillion lira at 52 percent overnight. But it lent 20.9 trillion lira at 67 percent via tmrw/next and 3.7 trillion lira at 68 percent via tmrw/week due to expected cash shortage for Monday, bankers said.
The average overnight money and repo rates dived to 56.26 and 69.75 percent from Thursday's 70.87 and 71.06 percent, respectively.
The bond market remained cautious amid political uncertainty mounting due to early poll possibility in 1997. Trade volume was low and the yields were mixed.
Bankers said the yields moved lower in short-term papers amid firmer demand but eased in longer-terms due to selling prompted by political concerns.

The most active paper was again April 22, 1998 which yielded 102.84 percent, up 0.62 percentage point from Thursday. The second was December 10, 1997, yielding 98.76 percent, down 0.09 percentage point.
"The newly issued two-year, inflation-indexed bonds began to be traded because their higher risk premium of 32 percent, compared to the previous issues", a private banker said.
The Treasury sold 236 trillion lira of two-year inflation-indexed bonds at 32 percent risk premium on Wednesday, up sharply from 29.95 percent on the previous similar issue on May 13.
Bankers said the 32 percent risk premium brought a return exceeding the overnight cost of funding, triggering demand for the new bonds.
Lira fell to 142,960 to the dollar compared to Thursday's close of 142,490 as the U.S. currency rose against the mark after Germany unemployment data was released.
